## Welcome to the Transportation Data Science Challenge! 🚦

Complete these interactive R exercises to test your skills in transportation planning and data analysis. Each exercise builds on real-world scenarios you'll encounter as a transportation professional.
:::

```{webr}
#| context: setup
#| include: false

# Sample transportation data
traffic_data <- data.frame(
  location = c("Main St", "Oak Ave", "Park Rd", "First St", "Center Blvd", "Highway 101"),
  aadt = c(15000, 8500, 12000, 6800, 22000, 45000),
  speed_limit = c(35, 25, 30, 25, 45, 65),
  lanes = c(4, 2, 3, 2, 6, 8),
  accidents_2023 = c(12, 3, 8, 2, 18, 35),
  congestion_hours = c(4, 2, 3, 1, 6, 8)
)

# Bike share data
bike_data <- data.frame(
  station = paste("Station", LETTERS[1:6]),
  daily_trips = c(45, 78, 23, 56, 89, 34),
  distance_downtown_km = c(0.5, 2.1, 4.2, 1.8, 0.8, 3.5),
  bike_capacity = c(20, 30, 15, 25, 35, 20)
)

# Transit data
transit_data <- data.frame(
  route = paste0("Route ", 1:5),
  daily_riders = c(1200, 850, 2100, 650, 1800),
  route_length_miles = c(12.5, 8.2, 18.3, 6.1, 15.7),
  frequency_minutes = c(15, 20, 10, 30, 12)
)

# Level of Service data
los_data <- data.frame(
  intersection = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"),
  delay_seconds = c(10, 25, 45, 75, 120),
  volume = c(800, 1200, 1600, 1800, 2000),
  capacity = c(1800, 1800, 1800, 1800, 1800)
)
```

```{pyodide}
#| context: setup
#| include: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

traffic_data = pd.DataFrame({
    "location": ["Main St", "Oak Ave", "Park Rd", "First St", "Center Blvd", "Highway 101"],
    "aadt": [15000, 8500, 12000, 6800, 22000, 45000],
    "speed_limit": [35, 25, 30, 25, 45, 65],
    "lanes": [4, 2, 3, 2, 6, 8],
    "accidents_2023": [12, 3, 8, 2, 18, 35],
    "congestion_hours": [4, 2, 3, 1, 6, 8],
})

bike_data = pd.DataFrame({
    "station": ["Station " + c for c in "ABCDEF"],
    "daily_trips": [45, 78, 23, 56, 89, 34],
    "distance_downtown_km": [0.5, 2.1, 4.2, 1.8, 0.8, 3.5],
    "bike_capacity": [20, 30, 15, 25, 35, 20],
})

transit_data = pd.DataFrame({
    "route": ["Route " + str(i) for i in range(1, 6)],
    "daily_riders": [1200, 850, 2100, 650, 1800],
    "route_length_miles": [12.5, 8.2, 18.3, 6.1, 15.7],
    "frequency_minutes": [15, 20, 10, 30, 12],
})

los_data = pd.DataFrame({
    "intersection": list("ABCDE"),
    "delay_seconds": [10, 25, 45, 75, 120],
    "volume": [800, 1200, 1600, 1800, 2000],
    "capacity": [1800] * 5,
})
```

## 🧠 **Knowledge Test**

*Test your understanding of transportation planning fundamentals*

### Question 1: Traffic Signal Timing ⏱️

If a traffic light has a 90-second cycle and the green light lasts 60 seconds, how many cars can pass through if each car takes 3 seconds to clear the intersection?

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

## {{< fa brands r-project >}} R

```{webr}
#| exercise: know_1
#| caption: "Knowledge Question 1"
# Calculate how many cars can pass in one green phase
green_time <- 60  # seconds
time_per_car <- 3  # seconds

# Your calculation:
cars_per_cycle <- ______

cars_per_cycle
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: know_1
#| check: true
# Custom feedback function
if (!exists("cars_per_cycle")) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚫 Please create the 'cars_per_cycle' variable and run your code.", type = "error")
} else if (identical(cars_per_cycle, 20)) {
  list(correct = TRUE, message = "🎯 Perfect! 20 cars can pass through in one green cycle. This is a fundamental capacity calculation used in traffic signal timing.", type = "success")
} else if (cars_per_cycle > 20) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "🤔 Too many cars! Remember, each car needs 3 seconds to clear the intersection. Try dividing the green time by the time per car.", type = "warning")
} else if (cars_per_cycle < 20) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚗 Not quite enough cars! How many 3-second periods fit in 60 seconds? Think: 60 ÷ 3 = ?", type = "info")
} else {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "🔢 Make sure your result is a number. Check your calculation.", type = "error")
}
```

### Question 2: Level of Service 🚦

Calculate the volume-to-capacity (V/C) ratio for an intersection with 1,600 vehicles/hour and capacity of 1,800 vehicles/hour. What LOS category does this represent? (A-C: ≤0.8, D: 0.8-0.9, E-F: >0.9)

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

## {{< fa brands r-project >}} R

```{webr}
#| exercise: know_2
#| caption: "Knowledge Question 2"
volume <- 1600
capacity <- 1800

# Calculate V/C ratio
vc_ratio <- ______

# Determine LOS category
los_category <- ______  # Should be "A-C", "D", or "E-F"

list(vc_ratio = vc_ratio, los_category = los_category)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: know_2
#| check: true
if (!exists("vc_ratio") || !exists("los_category")) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚫 Please create both 'vc_ratio' and 'los_category' variables.", type = "error")
} else {
  vc_correct <- round(vc_ratio, 3) == round(1600/1800, 3)
  los_correct <- los_category == "D"
  
  if (vc_correct && los_correct) {
    list(correct = TRUE, message = "🎯 Excellent! V/C = 0.889 puts this intersection at LOS D. This indicates approaching unstable flow with tolerable delays.", type = "success")
  } else if (!vc_correct && los_correct) {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "🔢 LOS category is correct, but check your V/C calculation: volume ÷ capacity = 1600 ÷ 1800", type = "warning")
  } else if (vc_correct && !los_correct) {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "📊 V/C ratio is correct (0.889), but check the LOS thresholds: 0.8-0.9 = Level D", type = "warning")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚦 Both calculations need work. V/C ratio = volume ÷ capacity, then check: ≤0.8=A-C, 0.8-0.9=D, >0.9=E-F", type = "error")
  }
}
```

### Question 3: Modal Split 🚌🚲🚗

In a city where 40% of trips are by car, 25% by transit, 20% by walking, and 15% by cycling, what percentage of non-car trips are made by transit?

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

## {{< fa brands r-project >}} R

```{webr}
#| exercise: know_3
#| caption: "Knowledge Question 3"
car_percent <- 40
transit_percent <- 25
walking_percent <- 20
cycling_percent <- 15

# Calculate percentage of non-car trips that are transit
non_car_total <- ______
transit_share_of_non_car <- ______

transit_share_of_non_car
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: know_3
#| check: true
if (!exists("transit_share_of_non_car")) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚫 Please create the 'transit_share_of_non_car' variable and run your code.", type = "error")
} else if (round(transit_share_of_non_car, 1) == 41.7) {
  list(correct = TRUE, message = "🚌 Perfect! 41.7% of non-car trips are made by transit. This shows transit's importance in the sustainable transportation mix.", type = "success")
} else if (transit_share_of_non_car == 25) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "🤔 That's the overall transit share (25%). But what about just among non-car trips? Hint: transit % ÷ non-car total % × 100", type = "info")
} else if (round(transit_share_of_non_car, 0) == 42) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚌 Very close! 41.7% of non-car trips are made by transit. Your calculation method is correct!", type = "warning")
} else {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "📊 Remember: First find non-car total (100 - car %), then calculate: (transit %) ÷ (non-car total %) × 100", type = "error")
}
```

### Question 4: Trip Generation 🏠

A residential development has 200 housing units. Using ITE trip generation rate of 9.5 trips per dwelling unit per day, calculate total daily trips. If 15% occur during PM peak hour, how many PM peak trips?

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

## {{< fa brands r-project >}} R

```{webr}
#| exercise: know_4
#| caption: "Knowledge Question 4"
housing_units <- 200
trip_rate <- 9.5
pm_peak_percent <- 15

# Calculate total daily trips
total_daily_trips <- ______

# Calculate PM peak hour trips  
pm_peak_trips <- ______

list(daily = total_daily_trips, pm_peak = pm_peak_trips)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: know_4
#| check: true
if (!exists("total_daily_trips") || !exists("pm_peak_trips")) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚫 Please create both 'total_daily_trips' and 'pm_peak_trips' variables.", type = "error")
} else {
  daily_correct <- total_daily_trips == 1900
  peak_correct <- pm_peak_trips == 285
  
  if (daily_correct && peak_correct) {
    list(correct = TRUE, message = "🏠 Excellent! 1,900 daily trips with 285 during PM peak. These are key numbers for traffic impact studies.", type = "success")
  } else if (!daily_correct && peak_correct) {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "🏘️ PM peak trips are correct, but check daily trips: units × trip rate = 200 × 9.5", type = "warning")
  } else if (daily_correct && !peak_correct) {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "🕔 Daily trips correct, but check PM peak: daily trips × 15% = 1900 × 0.15", type = "warning")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "📊 Both calculations need work. Daily = units × rate, PM peak = daily × 15%", type = "error")
  }
}
```

### Question 5: Transit Frequency 🚍

A bus route operates every 12 minutes during peak hours. How many buses pass a given stop in one hour? If each bus has 40-passenger capacity and average load is 75%, what's the hourly passenger capacity past that stop?

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

## {{< fa brands r-project >}} R

```{webr}
#| exercise: know_5
#| caption: "Knowledge Question 5"
frequency_minutes <- 12
bus_capacity <- 40
load_factor <- 0.75

# Calculate buses per hour
buses_per_hour <- ______

# Calculate hourly passenger capacity
hourly_passenger_capacity <- ______

list(buses_per_hour = buses_per_hour, hourly_capacity = hourly_passenger_capacity)
```


```{webr}
#| exercise: know_5
#| check: true
if (!exists("buses_per_hour") || !exists("hourly_passenger_capacity")) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚫 Please create both 'buses_per_hour' and 'hourly_passenger_capacity' variables.", type = "error")
} else {
  buses_correct <- buses_per_hour == 5
  capacity_correct <- hourly_passenger_capacity == 150
  
  if (buses_correct && capacity_correct) {
    list(correct = TRUE, message = "🚍 Perfect! 5 buses per hour with 150 passenger capacity. This helps determine route efficiency and passenger service levels.", type = "success")
  } else if (!buses_correct && capacity_correct) {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "🕒 Passenger capacity is correct, but check buses per hour: 60 minutes ÷ frequency = 60 ÷ 12", type = "warning")
  } else if (buses_correct && !capacity_correct) {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "👥 Buses per hour correct, but check capacity: buses × capacity × load factor = 5 × 40 × 0.75", type = "warning")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚌 Both calculations need work. Buses/hour = 60 ÷ frequency, Capacity = buses × seats × load factor", type = "error")
  }
}
```

## 🚀 **Skills Test**

*Put your R and dplyr skills to work with real transportation datasets*

### Question 1: High-Traffic Location Analysis 📊

Using the `traffic_data` dataset, filter for locations with AADT > 15,000 and count how many locations meet this criteria.

```{webr}
#| context: setup
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

## {{< fa brands r-project >}} R

```{webr}
#| autorun: true
#| caption: "Traffic Data"
# First, let's see the data
traffic_data
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: skill_1
#| caption: "Skill Question 1"
# Filter for high-traffic locations and count them
high_traffic <- traffic_data |>
  filter(______)

# Count the results
count_high_traffic <- ______

count_high_traffic
```


```{webr}
#| exercise: skill_1
#| check: true
# Custom feedback function
if (!exists("high_traffic") || !exists("count_high_traffic")) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "📊 Make sure to create both 'high_traffic' and 'count_high_traffic' variables.", type = "error")
} else {
  expected_high_traffic <- traffic_data |> filter(aadt > 15000)
  filter_correct <- identical(high_traffic, expected_high_traffic)
  count_correct <- count_high_traffic == nrow(expected_high_traffic)
  
  if (filter_correct && count_correct) {
    list(correct = TRUE, message = "🎯 Perfect! You correctly identified 3 high-traffic locations (Main St, Center Blvd, Highway 101) with AADT > 15,000. This type of analysis helps prioritize infrastructure investments.", type = "success")
  } else if (!filter_correct && count_correct) {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "🔍 Count is correct, but check your filtering condition. You should use: filter(aadt > 15000)", type = "warning")
  } else if (filter_correct && !count_correct) {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "📋 Filtering is correct, but check your count calculation. Use nrow() to count the filtered results.", type = "warning")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚗 Check both your filter condition (aadt > 15000) and count method (use nrow()).", type = "error")
  }
}
```

### Question 2: Safety Rate Calculation 🔍

### Question 3: Transit Efficiency Analysis 🚌

Calculate riders per mile for each transit route and identify the most efficient route (highest riders per mile).

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

## {{< fa brands r-project >}} R

```{webr}
transit_data
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: skill_3
#| caption: "Skill Question 3"
# Calculate efficiency and find the best route
transit_efficiency <- transit_data |>
  mutate(riders_per_mile = ______) |>
  arrange(______)

# Get the most efficient route name
most_efficient <- transit_efficiency |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(______)

most_efficient
```


```{webr}
#| exercise: skill_3
#| check: true
if (!exists("transit_efficiency") || !exists("most_efficient")) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "📊 Make sure to create both 'transit_efficiency' and 'most_efficient' variables.", type = "error")
} else {
  expected_efficiency <- transit_data |>
    mutate(riders_per_mile = daily_riders / route_length_miles) |>
    arrange(desc(riders_per_mile))
  expected_most_efficient <- expected_efficiency |> slice(1) |> pull(route)
  
  efficiency_correct <- identical(transit_efficiency, expected_efficiency)
  route_correct <- identical(most_efficient, expected_most_efficient)
  
  if (efficiency_correct && route_correct) {
    list(correct = TRUE, message = "🎯 Perfect! Route 3 is the most efficient with 114.8 riders per mile. This analysis helps transit agencies optimize route planning and resource allocation.", type = "success")
  } else if (!efficiency_correct && route_correct) {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚌 Most efficient route is correct, but check your efficiency calculation: daily_riders / route_length_miles", type = "warning")
  } else if (efficiency_correct && !route_correct) {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "📊 Efficiency calculation is correct, but check how you're extracting the most efficient route name using pull(route)", type = "warning")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚍 Check both your efficiency calculation (riders ÷ miles) and route extraction (slice(1) |> pull(route))", type = "error")
  }
}
```

```{webr}
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(

  ) +
```

```{pyodide}
# Add a linear trend line
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(bike_data["distance_downtown_km"], bike_data["daily_trips"], 1)
x_line = np.linspace(bike_data["distance_downtown_km"].min(), bike_data["distance_downtown_km"].max(), 50)
ax.plot(x_line, slope * x_line + intercept, color="red")

ax.set_title("Bike Share Usage vs Distance from Downtown")
ax.set_xlabel("Distance from Downtown (km)")
ax.set_ylabel("Daily Trips")
plt.show()
```

### Question 5: Comprehensive Performance Summary 🏆

Create a summary table showing for each location: total daily volume, accidents per 1000 vehicles, and congestion level (Low: <3hrs, Medium: 3-5hrs, High: >5hrs).

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

## {{< fa brands r-project >}} R

```{webr}
#| exercise: skill_5
#| caption: "Skill Question 5"
# Create comprehensive performance summary
performance_summary <- traffic_data |>
  mutate(
    daily_volume = ______,
    accidents_per_1000 = ______,
    congestion_level = case_when(
      ______ < 3 ~ "Low",
      ______ <= 5 ~ "Medium",
      TRUE ~ "High"
    )
  ) |>
  select(location, daily_volume, accidents_per_1000, congestion_level)

performance_summary
```


```{webr}
#| exercise: skill_5
#| check: true
if (!exists("performance_summary")) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "📊 Make sure to create the 'performance_summary' variable.", type = "error")
} else {
  expected_result <- traffic_data |>
    mutate(
      daily_volume = aadt,
      accidents_per_1000 = (accidents_2023 / aadt) * 1000,
      congestion_level = case_when(
        congestion_hours < 3 ~ "Low",
        congestion_hours <= 5 ~ "Medium", 
        TRUE ~ "High"
      )
    ) |>
    select(location, daily_volume, accidents_per_1000, congestion_level)
  
  expected_cols <- c("location", "daily_volume", "accidents_per_1000", "congestion_level")
  has_correct_cols <- all(expected_cols %in% names(performance_summary))
  
  if (!has_correct_cols) {
    missing_cols <- setdiff(expected_cols, names(performance_summary))
    list(correct = FALSE, message = paste("📋 Missing columns:", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")), type = "error")
  } else if (identical(performance_summary, expected_result)) {
    list(correct = TRUE, message = "🎯 Outstanding! You've created a comprehensive performance dashboard showing volume, safety rates, and congestion levels. This type of integrated analysis is essential for transportation planning and helps identify priority locations for improvements.", type = "success")
  } else {
    daily_vol_correct <- identical(performance_summary$daily_volume, expected_result$daily_volume)
    accidents_correct <- all(abs(performance_summary$accidents_per_1000 - expected_result$accidents_per_1000) < 0.001)
    congestion_correct <- identical(performance_summary$congestion_level, expected_result$congestion_level)
    
    if (!daily_vol_correct) {
      list(correct = FALSE, message = "📊 Check daily_volume calculation: should be the same as aadt", type = "warning")
    } else if (!accidents_correct) {
      list(correct = FALSE, message = "🔢 Check accidents_per_1000 calculation: (accidents_2023 / aadt) * 1000", type = "warning")
    } else if (!congestion_correct) {
      list(correct = FALSE, message = "🚦 Check congestion_level case_when logic: <3='Low', <=5='Medium', >5='High'", type = "warning")
    } else {
      list(correct = FALSE, message = "📋 Almost there! Check your mutate and select statements carefully.", type = "error")
    }
  }
}
```

```{pyodide}
            [______ < 3, ______ <= 5],

        ),
```

```{pyodide}
#| exercise: skill_5_py
#| check: true
if "performance_summary" not in envir_result:
    fb = {"correct": False, "message": "📊 Make sure to create the 'performance_summary' variable.", "type": "error"}
else:
    import numpy as np
    result = envir_result["performance_summary"]
    data = envir_result["traffic_data"]
    expected_cols = ["location", "daily_volume", "accidents_per_1000", "congestion_level"]
    missing_cols = [c for c in expected_cols if c not in result.columns]
    if missing_cols:
        fb = {"correct": False, "message": "📋 Missing columns: " + ", ".join(missing_cols), "type": "error"}
    else:
        daily_vol_correct = bool((result["daily_volume"] == data["aadt"]).all())
        accidents_correct = bool(np.allclose(result["accidents_per_1000"], data["accidents_2023"] / data["aadt"] * 1000, atol=0.001))
        expected_levels = np.select([data["congestion_hours"] < 3, data["congestion_hours"] <= 5], ["Low", "Medium"], default="High")
        congestion_correct = list(result["congestion_level"]) == list(expected_levels)
        if daily_vol_correct and accidents_correct and congestion_correct:
            fb = {"correct": True, "message": "🎯 Outstanding! You've created a comprehensive performance dashboard showing volume, safety rates, and congestion levels. This type of integrated analysis is essential for transportation planning and helps identify priority locations for improvements.", "type": "success"}
        elif not daily_vol_correct:
            fb = {"correct": False, "message": "📊 Check daily_volume calculation: should be the same as aadt", "type": "warning"}
        elif not accidents_correct:
            fb = {"correct": False, "message": "🔢 Check accidents_per_1000 calculation: (accidents_2023 / aadt) * 1000", "type": "warning"}
        else:
            fb = {"correct": False, "message": "🚦 Check congestion_level logic: <3='Low', <=5='Medium', >5='High'", "type": "warning"}
fb
```
